devious

DEE-vee-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Devious is willing to lie, trick, or use unfair tactics to get what one wants.

The chess opponent relied on a devious trick, deliberately mistiming the clock to rattle his rival's concentration.

Example

A coworker devised a devious plan to take sole credit for the group's project, quietly removing his teammates' names from the final report.

The coworker didn't just make a mistake -- he deliberately schemed and lied to benefit himself, exactly what devious describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

cunning: Cunning means skilled at getting what you want through clever, often deceptive planning -- it can even sound half-admiring. Devious is never a compliment: a devious person or plan relies on indirect tricks and unfair tactics, and the word always judges that winding route as dishonest.

underhanded: Underhanded describes the method itself: doing things secretly and dishonestly -- hidden fees, rigged raffles, whispered side deals. Devious is broader, describing a whole person or plan that reaches its goal by roundabout tricks. One underhanded move is a single dirty tactic; a devious schemer strings many together.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

honest: truthful and sincere

straightforward: direct and open, without hidden motives

Where it sits · how far the deceit will go — sly → devious → treacherous

sly vs. devious: Someone sly is a bit crafty or secretive, often in small ways, milder than fully devious.

treacherous vs. devious: Someone treacherous is willing to betray trust completely, an even more dangerous form of dishonesty than devious.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: away from (Latin)

Root — vi

Root — vi: road, way (from Latin via, 'road, way')

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Devious combines de- ("away from") + vi ("road, way," from Latin via) + -ous -- literally "off the road." Someone devious has wandered off the honest, straightforward path.

Use the root in a new word: via

Use the root in a new word: via: She sent the package via express mail so it would arrive by Friday.

Word Choice

Devious describes a person or plan willing to lie, trick, or manipulate -- a stronger, less neutral word than merely calling someone "clever" or "resourceful."
